site_program: POLAR study; 3 academic hospitals, 11 regional hospitals, 75 midwifery practices in Leiden-Amsterdam region
screening_population: asymptomatic newborns after exclusion of prenatally detected CCHD and CCHD presenting symptomatically immediately after birth; home births and early-discharge hospital births
screening_timing_raw: >=1 h after birth and again on day 2 or 3
screening_algorithm_raw: pre- and postductal SpO2; positive if <90% or if 2 independent measurements were <95% and/or pre/postductal difference >3%; positive screens referred for pediatric assessment
study_target_definition_raw: CCHD accuracy-study target used by POLAR; 5 pulse-oximetry-detected CCHD and 221 CCHD false-positive final screens
diagnosis_categories_raw: respiratory pathology; infection/sepsis; non-critical CHD; other pathology; healthy
diagnosis_counts_raw: respiratory pathology 88; infection/sepsis 31; non-critical CHD 3; other pathology 12; healthy 87
individual_diagnoses: respiratory pathology; infection/sepsis; non-critical CHD; other significant pathology; healthy
management_actionability_evidence: Primary report states that clinically significant noncardiac illnesses detected by screening led to early recognition and referral for treatment. The same-cohort author summary decomposes the 221 false positives into 88 respiratory, 31 infection/sepsis, 3 non-critical CHD, 12 other pathology, and 87 healthy. Strict coding therefore uses CAN-AB=131 for the noncardiac disease groups explicitly linked to referral/treatment; the 3 non-critical CHD are CAN-U because no concrete treatment/follow-up consequence is reported for that subgroup.
poolability_reason: complete 221-infant CCHD-negative classification; 131 have aggregate documented referral-for-treatment actionability; 3 clinically significant non-critical CHD lack subgroup-specific actionability and remain CAN-U; 87 explicitly healthy in same-cohort author summary
source_full_text_provenance: Primary: Narayen IC et al. J Pediatr. 2018;197:29-35.e1. PMID 29580679; DOI 10.1016/j.jpeds.2018.01.039. Supporting same-cohort author summary: Narayen IC, Blom NA, te Pas AB. Int J Neonatal Screen. 2018;4:11. PMCID PMC7510226.
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 131/221; Expanded 134/221; healthy 87/221. The 134 disease total is preserved; only the 3 non-critical CHD are withheld from Strict for lack of subgroup-specific management evidence.

site_program: Mohammed VI University Hospital maternity ward, Marrakesh
screening_timing_raw: before discharge; only 12% screened >24 h; most vaginal-delivery infants screened <24 h
screening_algorithm_raw: AAP pre/postductal pulse-oximetry algorithm; failed screens received urgent pediatric-cardiology examination and echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: authors classify 5 CCHD, 5 non-critical CHD, and 5 false positives
diagnosis_categories_raw: study-defined CCHD; non-critical CHD; PPHN; sepsis; normal
diagnosis_counts_raw: study-defined CCHD 5; non-critical CHD 5; PPHN 1; sepsis 2; normal 2
individual_diagnoses: study-defined CCHD: D-TGA 1; DORV+TGA+pulmonary stenosis 1; coarctation+PDA 1; HLHS 2. Non-critical: single atrium 1; hypertrophic myocardium 2; large ASD 1; AV canal 1. Other: PPHN 1; sepsis 2; normal 2
management_actionability_evidence: Two sepsis cases were diagnosed and treated early with good outcomes -> CAN-A=2. Single atrium, large ASD and AV canal were stable and waiting for surgery -> CAN-B=3. If either/both target-uncertain cardiac cases remain in the harmonized-CCHD-negative denominator, their planned surgery makes them CAN-B as well. PPHN had outcome 'normal' without a specific treatment consequence -> CAN-U=1. Two hypertrophic-myocardium findings resolved to 'normal heart' -> NON_CAN=2. Two normal findings -> explicitly healthy/no diagnosis=2.
poolability_reason: exact harmonized denominator cannot be point-identified: DORV+TGA+PS and CoA+PDA are study-defined CCHD but the source does not establish the <=28-day invasive-intervention/death criterion required by the locked harmonized target. Bounded sensitivity is fully classifiable without inventing timing.
source_full_text_provenance: Primary full text: El Idrissi Slitine N et al. Int J Neonatal Screen. 2020;6(3):53. PMID 33123634; PMCID PMC7570348; DOI 10.3390/ijns6030053.
extraction_notes: Harmonized denominator 10-12; Strict 5-7; Expanded 6-8. Corresponding Strict proportion range 50.0%-58.3%; Expanded range 60.0%-66.7%. No primary meta-analysis point weight is assigned.

screening_population: newborns >=35 weeks admitted to postnatal ward; antenatal CHD and NICU admissions excluded
screening_algorithm_raw: postductal pulse oximetry; saturation <95% triggered echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: CCHD detected by pulse oximetry; Cochrane 2018 harmonized-target extraction validates 7 TP and 7 FP
diagnosis_categories_raw: non-critical but significant CHD; previously undiagnosed respiratory illness or sepsis
individual_diagnoses: three significant non-critical CHD; four respiratory illness/sepsis
management_actionability_evidence: Primary report establishes clinically significant pathology in all 7 CCHD-negative failed screens but does not document specific treatment, escalation, altered disposition, or required follow-up for either subgroup. All 7 therefore map to CAN-U rather than Strict CAN-CCHD.
poolability_reason: complete diagnosis ascertainment; all 7 clinically relevant CCHD-negative outcomes are classifiable as CAN-U because actionability is not demonstrated in the accessible primary report
source_full_text_provenance: Primary: Oakley JL et al. J Matern Fetal Neonatal Med. 2015;28(14):1736-1739. PMID 25241768; DOI 10.3109/14767058.2014.967674. Harmonized target validation: Plana et al. Cochrane 2018, PMID 29494750, Oakley TP=7/FP=7.
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 0/7; Expanded 7/7. 'Significant' or 'unwell' is not substituted for specific actionability evidence.

site_program: St Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College, Addis Ababa
screening_population: apparently healthy term newborns with normal vital signs, no respiratory distress, active feeding, no murmur/diminished pulses; screened before discharge
screening_algorithm_raw: positive if SpO2 <90% in any extremity, or persistent 90%-94% in both sites on three measurements, or persistent arm-foot difference >3%; all 56 final positives underwent echocardiography
study_target_definition_raw: CCHD screening; no CCHD detected among final failed screens
diagnosis_categories_raw: PPHN; sepsis overlapping PPHN; PDA; ASD; no echocardiographic abnormality with clinically unremarkable pediatric reassessment
diagnosis_counts_raw: PPHN 10, including sepsis overlap in 2; PDA 11; ASD 2; no echo abnormality/clinically unremarkable 33
individual_diagnoses: PPHN 10; sepsis within 2 of the PPHN cases; PDA 11; ASD 2; no abnormality 33
management_actionability_evidence: All 10 PPHN infants were admitted to NICU and treated; 2 also had sepsis and were managed per hospital guideline, and PPHN resolved -> CAN-A=10 without double-counting sepsis. PDA 11 and ASD 2 had other causes of hypoxemia excluded, were monitored until SpO2 normalized, discharged with explicit follow-up advice -> CAN-B=13 under the locked rule allowing minor lesions to become actionable when qualifying follow-up is documented. The 33 echo-negative infants were re-evaluated by a pediatrician, had unremarkable clinical findings, normalized SpO2 and were sent home -> explicitly healthy/no diagnosis=33.
poolability_reason: complete participant-level clinical ascertainment and management evidence; retain high-altitude and predominantly early-screen timing as prespecified heterogeneity/subgroup flags
source_full_text_provenance: Primary full text: Tekleab AM, Sewnet YC. Pediatr Health Med Ther. 2019;10:83-88. PMID 31616201; PMCID PMC6699584; DOI 10.2147/PHMT.S217987.
extraction_notes: Strict CAN-CCHD 23/56; Expanded 23/56; explicitly healthy/no diagnosis 33/56. PPHN/sepsis overlap is counted once at participant level. Altitude 2600 m must be preserved in subgroup/sensitivity analysis.
